content.comment_body: Hello, I am using [product_name] software [product_name] V5.0.21. I have five up/down counters, and I want to display both the current threshold and counter values on one line of the [product_name] screen. However, the input in the message text box is not being accepted, likely because there is one character too many to fit everything on a single line. Does anyone have a tip on how to display both values on one line? I could split over two screens, but having everything on one line would be best if possible. Thanks for any help!

Hello [user_name], With the older type of [product_name] controllers ([article_no] and earlier), it's not possible to place more than one live value in a textbox on a single line. The manual for the newer model ([article_no]) doesn't mention how many live block values you can put in one textbox line (note: the line can have 24 characters). There is a workaround for displaying two small current values in one textbox line. Check the attachment for an example: it shows a user-created counter for time in hours and minutes. On the second page, there's a circuit using a comparator, which helps combine two integers (e.g. 0..327 and 0..99) separated by a decimal point, forming a pseudo-decimal value (in the format "0.00" to "327.99") for display. Here, the decimal serves as a separator between the two numbers. Hope this is useful!

Hello [user_name], You described it as a trick, but it seems almost magical! I can't use it for my application since my counter goes above 327, but I learned a lot from your explanation. Thanks for sharing your insight!
Hello [user_name], Thank you for your response! Glad to hear my post was helpful.

analysis.insight_summary: The user faces a limitation with [product_name] display and [product_name] software V5, struggling to show both threshold and counter values together on a single display line due to text box character limits. Creative formatting is possible for small values, but doesn't help with larger numbers, highlighting both hardware and software constraints and a desire for more flexible display options.
